description: Photograph/scan of an unclassified September 29, 2020 letter from Director of National Intelligence John Ratcliffe to Senator Lindsey Graham, Chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee. The letter declassifies IC information related to the FBI's Crossfire Hurricane investigation, describing Russian intelligence analysis alleging Hillary Clinton approved a plan to tie Donald Trump to Russian hacking; the letter itself notes the IC does not know the accuracy of the allegation. Signed in blue ink by John Ratcliffe.
text: UNCLASSIFIED. DIRECTOR OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE. WASHINGTON, DC. SEP 29 2020. The Honorable Lindsey Graham. Chairman, Committee on the Judiciary. United States Senate. 290 Russell Senate Office Building. Washington, D.C. 20510. Chairman Graham,. In response to your request for Intelligence Community (IC) information related to the Federal Bureau of Investigation's (FBI) Crossfire Hurricane Investigation, I have declassified the following:. In late July 2016, U.S. intelligence agencies obtained insight into Russian intelligence analysis alleging that U.S. Presidential candidate Hillary Clinton had approved a campaign plan to stir up a scandal against U.S. Presidential candidate Donald Trump by tying him to Putin and the Russians' hacking of the Democratic National Committee. The IC does not know the accuracy of this allegation or the extent to which the Russian intelligence analysis may reflect exaggeration or fabrication. According to his handwritten notes, former Central Intelligence Agency Director Brennan subsequently briefed President Obama and other senior national security officials on the intelligence, including the "alleged approval by Hillary Clinton on July 26, 2016 of a proposal from one of her foreign policy advisors to vilify Donald Trump by stirring up a scandal claiming interference by Russian security services.". On 07 September 2016, U.S. intelligence officials forwarded an investigative referral to FBI Director James Comey and Deputy Assistant Director of Counterintelligence Peter Strzok regarding "U.S. Presidential candidate Hillary Clinton's approval of a plan concerning U.S. Presidential candidate Donald Trump and Russian hackers hampering U.S. elections as a means of distracting the public from her use of a private mail server.". As referenced in his 24 September 2020 letter to your Committee, Attorney General Barr has advised that the disclosure of this information will not interfere with ongoing Department of Justice investigations. Additional declassification and public disclosure of related intelligence remains under consideration; however, the IC welcomes the opportunity to provide a classified briefing with further detail at your convenience. Respectfully,. John Ratcliffe. UNCLASSIFIED
orgs: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
flags: The letter relays a Russian intelligence allegation about Hillary Clinton that the letter itself says the IC cannot verify and may be exaggerated or fabricated

description: Screenshot of an email exchange dated February 26, 2016 between Jennifer Palmieri (jpalmieri@hillaryclinton.com) and Joel Johnson (Joel@gpg.com), consistent with an email published in the leaked Podesta emails. Johnson asks who is in charge of 'the Trump swift boat project,' saying it needs to be ready, funded and unleashed; Palmieri replies sarcastically. Part of Johnson's message is highlighted in yellow by whoever shared the screenshot.
text: > On Feb 26, 2016, at 8:36 PM, Jennifer Palmieri <jpalmieri@hillaryclinton.com> wrote:. >. > Gee. Thanks, Joel. We thought we could half-ass it. Let's discuss.. >. > Sent from my iPhone. >. >> On Feb 26, 2016, at 8:35 PM, Joel Johnson <Joel@gpg.com> wrote:. >>. >> I know you can't look past Bernie and March primaries -- but who is in charge of the Trump swift boat project? Needs to be ready, funded and unleashed when we decide -- but not a half assed scramble.. >>. >> Sent from my iPhone
flags: Screenshot of a purportedly leaked email; authenticity and completeness of this rendering cannot be verified from the image alone

description: Screenshot of a one-page court letter (Case 1:19-cv-09420-RWL, Document 45, filed 09/30/20) from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York in The New York Times Company v. U.S. Department of State et al. AUSA Andrew E. Krause informs Magistrate Judge Robert W. Lehrburger that he is leaving the U.S. Attorney's Office and that AUSA Lucas Issacharoff will handle the case, submitted under Acting U.S. Attorney Audrey Strauss. A '1 of 1' overlay appears at top left.
text: Case 1:19-cv-09420-RWL Document 45 Filed 09/30/20 Page 1 of 1. 1 of 1. U.S. Department of Justice. United States Attorney. Southern District of New York. 86 Chambers Street. New York, New York 10007. September 30, 2020. By ECF. Honorable Robert W. Lehrburger. United States Magistrate Judge. United States Courthouse. 500 Pearl Street, Room 1960. New York, NY 10007. Re: The New York Times Company v. U.S. Department of State et al., 19 Civ. 9420 (RWL). Dear Judge Lehrburger:. I write respectfully to inform the Court that I will be leaving the United States Attorney's Office. Accordingly, I request the entry of an order terminating my appearance in this matter. My colleague, AUSA Lucas Issacharoff, has entered an appearance on behalf of the defendants and will continue to handle the case.. I thank the Court for its consideration of this submission.. Respectfully submitted,. AUDREY STRAUSS. Acting United States Attorney for the. Southern District of New York. By: /s/ Andrew E. Krause. ANDREW E. KRAUSE. Assistant United States Attorney. Telephone: 212-637-2769. Facsimile: 212-637-2786. E-mail: andrew.krause@usdoj.gov. cc: All counsel of record via ECF
orgs: U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York

description: Screenshot of a September 30, 2020 tweet from the pseudonymous account 'Nurse Deplorable' (@rn__deplorable) reacting to the SDNY attorney substitution in the NYT v. State Department case. The tweet claims Lucas Issacharoff is James Comey's son-in-law, married to Maurene Comey. It embeds two phone screenshots: a 'Biography Pedia' page about Maurene Comey describing her as Comey's daughter and lead prosecutor in the Jeffrey Epstein case, and a partial heavy.com page with a photo of a man in glasses at a formal event. The tweet's wording ('US Attorney of SDNY steps down') mischaracterizes the filing, which concerned an Assistant U.S. Attorney's withdrawal.
